findings.title: rowsAffected==0 wrongly treated as device limit reached on MySQL / unchanged rows
findings.body: updateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached whenever the UPDATE affects 0 rows. With MySQL (default CLIENT_FOUND_ROWS off) an UPDATE that matches an existing row but sets identical values reports 0 affected rows, so an already-registered anonymous device whose client_ip/user_agent/updated_at are unchanged would be denied authentication even though it is within the limit. The error is also semantically wrong for the 'device not found' case; a known device should succeed. Consider checking existence explicitly (SELECT) instead of relying on rows affected.

findings.title: localCache is populated before the store write, letting over-limit devices bypass the limit
findings.body: tagDeviceUI calls a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{}) before CreateOrUpdateDevice. If the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached (and the request is therefore rejected in Anonymous.Authenticate), the device id is nevertheless cached, so for the next ~29 minutes tagDeviceUI returns nil early and the same unknown device is granted anonymous access without ever being recorded. The limit is effectively bypassed by retrying. The cache should only be set after a successful write.

findings.title: Count-then-insert is not atomic, limit can be exceeded
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice reads the device count and then inserts in a separate statement/session. Concurrent anonymous requests (or multiple Grafana instances sharing the DB) can all observe count < deviceLimit and each insert, so the stored device count can exceed the configured device_limit. A transaction with appropriate locking, or an atomic INSERT ... SELECT guarded by the count, is needed if the limit is meant to be enforced.

findings.title: Device tagging moved onto the request path adds a DB count+write per anonymous request
findings.body: TagDevice was previously executed in a background goroutine with its own timeout; it is now called synchronously inside Authenticate. For every anonymous request that misses the local cache this now performs a SELECT COUNT(*) on anon_device plus an upsert before the request can proceed, and any DB latency/failure directly affects anonymous page loads. Under high anonymous traffic with a configured limit this COUNT query over a large table is a notable added cost.

findings.title: Raw ErrDeviceLimitReached returned from Authenticate yields an unhelpful 500/opaque error
findings.body: ErrDeviceLimitReached is created with fmt.Errorf and returned directly from Authenticate. The authn layer expects typed errutil errors to produce a correct HTTP status and user-facing message; a plain error will surface as a generic internal error rather than a clear 'anonymous device limit reached' response, and gives no way for the frontend to show the limit message implied by the new anonymousDeviceLimit frontend setting.

findings.title: New auth.anonymous device_limit option not documented in defaults.ini/sample.ini or docs
findings.body: cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit is read from [auth.anonymous] device_limit, but no entry was added to conf/defaults.ini, conf/sample.ini, or the configuration docs. Users have no discoverable way to learn about the setting or its default (0 = unlimited), and Grafana convention is that every ini option is listed in defaults.ini.

findings.title: ProvideAnonDBStore signature change may break wire DI registration
findings.body: ProvideAnonDBStore now takes an extra int64 argument and AnonDeviceService constructs the store itself instead of receiving anonstore.AnonStore. If ProvideAnonDBStore is still registered as a provider in pkg/server/wire.go (not included in this PR), wire will fail to build because there is no provider for int64, and any other consumer of the injected AnonStore loses it. Verify the DI graph was updated.

findings.title: Device limit tests do not cover the update path for an existing device at the limit
findings.body: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only asserts that a *new* device id is rejected once the limit is hit. There is no test that an already-registered device still succeeds (updates its updated_at/client_ip) when the limit is reached — exactly the path that is broken by the rowsAffected==0 logic on MySQL/unchanged rows. Add a case re-tagging the existing device id after the limit is reached.
